sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Endowment Management for Philanthropic and Scientific Grants

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (with EU-harmonised commercial, AML/CFT and company law overlay; Hague Apostille Convention of 5 October 1961 applies)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom DTA (1967, with 2009 and 2020 Protocols)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; CSSF Regulation No. 12-02; Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on annual accounts, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificat de non-faillite) of the general partner and corporate founders
Certified extract of corporate registry records of any foreign corporate partner or founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the foreign partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if source country is a Hague member; otherwise Consular Legalization via Luxembourg Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified passport copies and proof of residential address of all partners, UBOs and authorised signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority / municipal population registry of the individual's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for certified true copies; originals may be produced to a Luxembourg notary without apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional KYC package for each subscribing partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Credit institution in Luxembourg or the partner's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required; bank-to-bank confirmation to the Luxembourg notary or fiduciary is accepted

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Independent valuation report for any in-kind contribution to the SCSp (endowment assets)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille not required; original signed report delivered directly to the notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory adverse-media, PEP and sanctions screening of all partners, UBOs, general partner entities, directors and authorised signatories against: (i) FATF Recommendations; (ii) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (EU Regulation 269/2014 and EU Regulation 2580/2001); (iii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) OFAC SDN List; and (v) national Luxembourg RBE/AML databases and CSSF guidance. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for any individual or entity resident in a FATF grey-listed or EU high-risk third country, or where philanthropic counterpart funding originates from a foreign state organ.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers e-Registry (lbr.lu) – RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The RCS accepts legal entity names in French, German or English. The selected name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not be misleading as to the legal form or the intended activity. Where the name uses non-Latin script, a Latin-script transliteration must be filed concurrently. For an SCSp, the name may be followed by the abbreviation 'SCSp' or 'S.C.Sp.' to identify the legal form; the term 'Fondation' or 'Foundation' is not permitted in the SCSp name because the entity will retain partnership form.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce / Chamber of Commerce
Luxembourg / Grand-Duché (where implying official state function)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS does not operate a statutory name reservation; the pre-filing availability search is valid for a 30-day practical window between search and notarisation. Upon a negative clearance decision, the applicant may file a written reasoned request for reconsideration to the RCS department within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice. If the refusal is maintained, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg Tribunal administratif within 3 months, citing the naming provisions of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and on annual accounts, as amended. Where rejection concerns a sensitive token, a prior ministerial derogation may be requested from the Ministry of Justice, and the derogation letter must be appended to the notarised partnership deed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted only through a professional domiciliation agent licensed by the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of commercial companies. The agent must hold a physical Luxembourg registered office address and provide mail forwarding and governance contact facilities. A pure virtual office without a regulated domiciliation mandate is not acceptable for an SCSp engaged in philanthropic endowment management.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% quantified likelihood within the first 36 months, reflecting the low-risk charitable endowment profile; inspection may be triggered by adverse media, unusual transaction patterns, discrepancies between RBE filings, or irregular grant distributions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for electronic search via LBR portal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: EUR 2,900–3,800 for a standard SCSp deed including supporting corporate documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RBE registration fee applicable to SCSp entities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Luxembourg law firm or regulated fiduciary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per partner-UBO bundle, including PEP, OFAC, UN and EU sanctions screening and risk rating

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk vehicle: EUR 1,000–1,500 per annum, pro-rated for pre-incorporation period

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation, apostille and consular legalization batch for foreign KYC originals
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and competent apostille services in source jurisdictions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing consular and apostille tariffs in relevant source countries

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial ownership screening against UN, EU, OFAC and PEP lists (software and manual overlay)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance software vendor and reviewing counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per screened entity and per screened individual

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 94-1 et seq. concerning the Société en Commandite Spéciale) and Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Business Registers, as amended
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés – RCS), eJustice portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / Contrat de société de la Société en Commandite Spéciale
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital; capital and contributions are freely determined in the partnership agreement, and no escrow account is required under Luxembourg law
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned general partner, acting as the initial management organ of the Société en Commandite Spéciale, hereby: (1) confirms the subscription of all initial partnership interests by the partners in accordance with the partnership agreement; (2) adopts the registered office at the specified address in Luxembourg and instructs the registrar to file the registered office notice; (3) appoints the undersigned general partner and any designated individuals as managing partners with full authority to open bank accounts, execute grant distribution agreements, and appoint agents; (4) authorises submission of the incorporation instrument to the Luxembourg Business Registers and all ancillary filings; and (5) ratifies all pre-incorporation acts. This resolution takes effect immediately with the consent of all partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if real property contribution or desired authentication) or the partners themselves by private deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the partnership agreement in French or English setting out the identity of the general partner and limited partners, contribution schedule, profit-sharing rules, governance, and the purpose of managing a private charitable endowment. Execute before a notary when a partner contributes immovable property; otherwise execute as a private deed. Ensure all signatures are authenticated where required for RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of all general and limited partners
Consent of the proposed statutory auditor (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the deed, convene a partner meeting to amend the partnership agreement by notarial or private deed and resubmit with a letter of explanation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgement of the Incorporation Instrument with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS), eJustice online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership agreement and required appendices through the eJustice single point of entry. Pay the applicable registration and publication fees. The RCS examines the instrument for formal compliance with the Law of 10 August 1915.
required_dossiers: Residence and identification documents of the general partner
List of initial limited partners with contribution amounts
Power of attorney for the filing agent (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct formal deficiencies indicated by the RCS by filing an additional act or rectifying declaration; no new subscription is required unless contributions vary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration and Publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Official Journal (RCS – Mémorial C / RES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the RCS assigns a registration number and effects publication of the incorporation summary in the electronic gazette. The SCSp obtains legal standing for dealings with third parties from the date of registration, subject to statutory publication rules.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request administrative correction through the RCS register if details published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés are inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Business Identification Number and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically assigns the Luxembourg business registration number (OID). Register with the AEDT only if the SCSp is engaged in taxable transactions; for purely passive endowment management and grant distribution, VAT registration is unnecessary. Also obtain a tax file number from the Administration des contributions directes.
required_dossiers: List of representatives with identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, contact the AEDT taxpayer services with a copy of the RCS extract and request the OID-linked tax reference.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Beneficial Owner Declaration and Post-Registration Governance Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the beneficial owner declaration within one month of registration, identifying the natural persons holding interests in the SCSp. If the SCSp employs staff, register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale and complete the employer enrolment form. For any office premises, carry out local business licensure formalities.
required_dossiers: Identification documents for each beneficial owner
Lease or occupancy evidence for registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of a refusal, file a rectification letter with supporting evidence of ownership and chain of control; administrative penalty is avoidable by curing the omission within the prescribed period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Justice – Civil and Commercial Affairs (Ministère de la Justice), in coordination with the Luxembourg Business Registers for authorisation of public-benefit grant-making activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Declaration / Authorisation to Carry Out Public or Charitable Grant-Making Activities (Autorisation de distribution de libéralités philanthropiques)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no full EIA required; purely financial and office-based endowment management poses no substantial environmental impact
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emissions generated; office waste must be handled under the Luxembourg Code de l'Environnement; no effluent discharge permits applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for any occupied office premises issued by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS); structural load inspection and workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for office workstations and emergency exits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg Direct Tax Authority; online portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu. VAT registration and collection are administered by the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident entity or a newly formed SCSp without an existing Luxembourg tax identification number must register through MyGuichet.lu or via the RCS desk, requesting a Luxembourg national tax number (N° d'identification). For VAT, the entity must file a VAT registration application with the AEDT before making taxable supplies, obtaining an individual Luxembourg VAT number. The SCSp is not required to obtain a corporate income tax number for fiscally transparent earnings, but partners are identified for tax reporting through partner-level declarations. Non-resident partners with no Luxembourg-filing facts generally require no separate Luxembourg TIN unless direct Luxembourg-source income is derived or registration is otherwise triggered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election. An SCSp is statutorily fiscally transparent: it is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or net wealth tax as an entity, and its partners are taxed directly on their distributive share. The partners may govern allocation and profit-sharing by the partnership agreement, subject to Luxembourg anti-abuse and ATAD hybrid-mismatch rules. A SCSp is generally a separate taxable person for VAT purposes where it performs taxable economic activities; no partnership-level transparent exemption applies to VAT. Luxembourg VAT grouping is available in defined circumstances, but a SCSp cannot elect full entity-level CIT treatment unless the tax-transparent status is excluded by explicit legal provision, treaty override, or restructuring into a nontransparent vehicle.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) – Luxembourg VAT law
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Resident taxable persons carrying on economic activity must register for VAT when annual taxable turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 (small-enterprise exemption). Non-resident suppliers supplying goods by distance sale to Luxembourg consumers are required to register once EU-wide distance sales exceed EUR 10,000, or immediately for non-established suppliers making taxable supplies of services or goods without an exemption; pure passive endowment management and the distribution of grants by a charitable SCSp, when made without consideration, are not taxable supplies and do not trigger VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not impose real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping. Standard e-invoicing is mandatory only for business-to-government (B2G) transactions through Peppol-compliant channels. B2B invoicing may be electronic if the customer agrees, and invoices must be issued within 15 days after the chargeable event. No pre-clearance API transmission to the AEDT is required before invoice issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically transported by the supplier or a third party from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT rate provided the supplier retains objective transport and contractual evidence. Services directly related to exported goods, including handling, freight, and ancillary logistic services, may likewise be zero-rated where the ultimate benefit is in the foreign destination. Intra-EU supplies to a VAT-registered customer in another Member State are zero-rated with a valid EU VAT ID and periodic EC sales list declaration. Pure charitable grant distributions and non-economic endowment activities fall outside the scope of VAT and therefore do not amount to zero-rated supplies unless separately invoiced as services for consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD/Douane Luxembourg) with Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), CMR (road), or rail consignment note evidencing physical export from the EU
Commercial invoice and underlying supply contract
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer statement evidencing payment by the non-EU customer
Customs broker certification or power of attorney where the clearance is delegated
Supporting grant agreement, endowment deed, or beneficiary documentation showing the foreign recipient and purpose where services are supplied in connection with charitable activities
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Erroneous or fraudulent export zero-rating claims expose the taxpayer to assessment of the unpaid Luxembourg VAT at the standard rate of 17%, default interest of 0.8% per commenced month, administrative fines, and clawback of refunds for a period of up to five years under the VAT limitation statute. Intentional evasion or documentary falsification may be prosecuted as VAT fraud, attracting criminal penalties, personal director liability for the tax loss, and mandatory disclosure to the AEDT and public prosecutor. Misuse of charitable endowment status alongside false export documentation may additionally trigger revocation of any applicable exemption or fund license, restoration and clawback actions by the supervisory body, and AML or foundation-law sanctions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF). Luxembourg does not operate a discretionary foreign exchange approval regime; foreign exchange policy is anchored by the European Central Bank, while BCL compiles balance-of-payments statistics and administers statistical reporting under EU Regulation (EC) No 184/2005 and BCL Circular 2013/268. The CSSF exercises prudential supervision over licensed banks and payment institutions and enforces AML/CFT obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro and all other major currencies are fully convertible. Luxembourg implements the EU free movement of capital and payments regime under Articles 63 to 65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Capital Movements Directive 88/361/EEC. There is no distinction between current and capital account convertibility for a Luxembourg SCSp; capital contributions, endowment inflows, grant disbursements, and profit remittances require no authorisation, exchange permit, or quantitative limit. Applied restrictions arise only from EU and United Nations sanctions, targeted financial restrictive measures, and AML/CFT screening obligations. As the SCSp is tax-transparent under Luxembourg law, no withholding tax or profit-remittance barrier is imposed at the entity level, provided the partnership has no Luxembourg permanent establishment generating taxable commercial profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio. A Luxembourg-resident entity, including an SCSp, may retain export earnings, donations, or any inbound capital in the original currency without obligation to exchange into euro. The only compliance burden is the BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting obligation, which requires transactions in excess of the thresholds published in BCL Circulars to be filed on the 'Report-It-ONCE' electronic platform. Non-compliance may attract administrative penalties but never a currency conversion liability.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR/USD account with dedicated capital-escrow sub-ledger
Capital Escrow Account and Multi-Currency Operating Account
Operating Account with custody wallet for endowment securities and fixed-income assets
Private-wealth capital escrow and philanthropic grant-disbursement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for offshore or non-EU electronic money institutions. A charity endowment SCSp requires a full-service credit institution able to hold segregated multi-currency balances, execute SWIFT cross-border payments, issue documentary credit instruments where necessary, and support the CSSF substance expectations of regulated philanthropic vehicles. Luxembourg-authorised EMIs operating under the PSD2 passport provide only limited payment-account and money-remittance services and cannot provide commercial custody, treasury credit lines, or correspondent-banking access. Offshore EMIs, in particular, present unacceptable regulatory and jurisdictional risk and will not satisfy KYC due diligence or substance requirements. Such EMIs may be used solely as auxiliary collection points, never as the primary liquidity or settlement rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is not an absolute statutory precondition in Luxembourg, but in practical bank policy the general partner and each natural-person ultimate beneficial owner holding more than 25 percent is normally required to complete an onboarding interview, either in person or by certified video-conference compliant with CSSF Circular 20/732. For non-EEA residents, banks generally insist on a verified video session supplemented by notarised or apostilled identity documents and, in higher-risk cases, a face-to-face meeting with a legal or corporate-services representative. A Luxembourg registered office, a resident independent director, and a fully executed partnership deed meaningfully reduce the likelihood of refusal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp with entirely non-resident partners and limited local substance; bank flags a potential shell-feeder or financial pass-through arrangement.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Luxembourg notarial or private deed creating the SCSp; RCSL excerpt and up-to-date registration; UBO declaration filed on the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); audited opening balance sheet or audited endowment statement; local substance memorandum detailing registered office, authorised manager, bank signatories, and accounting service provider; signed capital commitment schedule from each limited partner; and a narrative grant and investment mandate explaining the non-commercial, philanthropic purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Grant or endowment flows to a jurisdiction subject to EU or UN restrictive measures or characterised by elevated money-laundering and terrorist-financing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written sanctions and embargo-compliancy policy; negative media and World-Check/Refinitiv screening results for every beneficiary and donor; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for donors; certified grant agreements containing purpose restrictions, beneficiary due diligence, and audit clauses; independent money-laundering risk assessment for each high-risk jurisdiction; and a signed undertaking by the general partner to block any prohibited payment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual concentration of significant philanthropic contributions immediately before account opening, without an identifiable donor track record or economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised or legalised donor commitment letters, bank references issued by the donor's home institution, and contribution side-letters referencing the fund's charitable mission; certified organisational chart demonstrating the independent foundation or trust origin of capital; the irrevocable endowment deed establishing the charitable purpose of the SCSp; up-to-date audited financials of the donor entity; and proof of the donor's own AML/KYC compliance framework if the donor is itself a regulated entity or public charity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections into the Luxembourg SCSp must be executed by SWIFT MT103 single credit transfer or, for high-value transactions, by MT202 COV with detailed beneficiary information. The remitting bank must include the SCSp's full legal name, RCSL registration number, and a purpose code indicating a capital contribution or endowment commitment, together with the reference of the relevant limited partnership agreement clause. The Luxembourg receiving bank will classify the credit under the BCL's balance-of-payments statistical categories and will request the capital commitment schedule, the board or general partner resolution, and confirmation that the paying bank is the account-holding institution of the contributing partner or donor. Compliance is completed when the receiving bank verifies that the incoming funds match the executed deed of contribution and that no sanctions or AML indicators exist on any party to the payment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Grant disbursements and operational outflows are cleared via SWIFT MT103 wires executed from the SCSp's Luxembourg account to the beneficiary's first-class bank. For commercial trade settlements undertaken by any commercial subsidiary of the endowment, banks in Luxembourg may issue SWIFT MT700 documentary letters of credit, MT707 amendments, or documentary collections under UCP 600. The SCSp itself is principally a grant-making endowment vehicle, so payables are executed using TARGET2 for euro clearing, SEPA Instant where relevant, and CHAPS or Fedwire via correspondent institutions for sterling and U.S. dollar payments. Every outbound instruction must carry the beneficiary's legal name, full address, unique identifier where available, and the grant or commercial reference, enabling the bank to satisfy the CSSF travel-rule and money-laundering reporting obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable FX forwards in major convertible currencies (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF, USD/JPY)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or thin-liquidity currencies (CNH, INR, BRL, TRY) subject to bank credit approval
Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) for exchanging fixed or floating cash flows between euro and U.S. dollar endowment asset portfolios
Over-the-counter vanilla FX options purchased solely for hedging endowment exposure, not for speculative proprietary trading

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Registration Data (Confirmation Annuelle) with the Luxembourg Business Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS / LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month following the anniversary of the initial RCS registration date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the entity to administrative fines of up to EUR 500 (approx USD 550) per delay; repeated non-compliance for more than two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off of the entity from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Beneficial Owner Information (Déclaration annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs) to the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one (1) month following the anniversary of the initial RBE registration / entity registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violations may result in criminal fines from EUR 125 to EUR 25,000 (approx USD 140 - USD 27,500); non-filing may trigger separate administrative enforcement and lead to RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (comptes annuels) submission to the RCS for publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Register (RCS) upon approval by the partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven (7) months of the financial year end (if 31 December year-end, due by 31 July of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can give rise to administrative fines of EUR 50 (approx USD 55) per day of delay, and the RCS may request judicial strike-off after two consecutive years of non-filing; partners/managers may be held personally liable.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required if an SCSp exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: (i) balance sheet total EUR 6,200,000 (approx USD 6,800,000); (ii) net turnover EUR 12,800,000 (approx USD 14,000,000); (iii) average number of employees 250. Charitable endowment entities that receive public subsidies or are constituted as public-interest may be subject to mandatory audit irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on annual accounts (transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU). IFRS may be adopted voluntarily or when consolidated listing status mandates it.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner of the SCSp must file, each year within one month after the anniversary of the entity's registration, a declaration with the RBE confirming the beneficial owners and their percentage of voting rights or ownership interest (any direct or indirect ownership exceeding 25%, or control via other means). Changes arising from shareholding transfers must be reported within one month of the change.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 900 per annum for a standard registered office and domestic agent in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 15,000 per annum for a mandatory independent audit of a small charitable endowment entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT (IRC), plus 7% solidarity surcharge and 6.75% municipal business tax in Luxembourg City, producing a 24.94% aggregate effective headline rate for CIT-subject entities; the SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and therefore subject to 0% entity-level corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is tax-transparent and not within Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax or net wealth tax at the vehicle level. Taxable income and losses flow through to partners, who bear tax at their own rates. A Luxembourg qualifying charitable foundation may apply for public-benefit exemption/agrément, but the selected SCSp structure does not itself enjoy a statutory CIT holiday; the participation exemption regime remains available to CIT-subject partners for qualifying dividend income (10% minority holding / 12-month holding period or 6% minimum holding ≥ 12 months as applicable).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 111 (Déclaration pour l’impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed through MyGuichet / e-Tax, the Luxembourg electronic filing portal of the Administration des contributions directes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year taxpayers, the return must be filed no later than 31 December of the year following the accounting year; periods based on a non-calendar fiscal year-end carry a filing deadline aligned to the end of the following corresponding accounting period unless the tax office sets an earlier notice deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg tax file number, address and statutory representative’s identity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner must not be inserted as a taxpayer on Form 111 unless the partner is separately assessed on Luxembourg-source business income through a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss per audited/approved financial statements before tax reconciliation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SCSp, leave blank; the commercial result is reported at partner level through Form 112 allocation, not in a collective Form 111.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg-taxable income after adding back non-deductible expenses and applying participation exemption, withholding taxes and treaty-based adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use only when the non-resident partner has a Luxembourg establishment or the SCSp is treated as taxable; treaty non-residents with no Luxembourg PE should not enter income here.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing and omission: automatic 10% tax surcharge, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% (capped at 10%), administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, and criminal penalties in cases of intentional failure to file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 112 – annual partnership declaration (Déclaration pour les sociétés de personnes) filed via MyGuichet / e-Tax for fiscally transparent partnerships and SCSp vehicles.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The partnership return follows the same annual filing cycle as Form 111: ordinarily 31 December following the accounting year for calendar-year entities; the Luxembourg tax administration may grant a six-month extension upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete identity, tax residence, share of capital, profit-sharing ratio and management rights of each general partner and special limited partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert each non-resident partner’s foreign tax identification number, residence certificate details and address to support application of an applicable double tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate gross income, deductible expenses, net profit/loss per partner and allocation based on the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocations must be made only for the period of partnership; a non-resident limited partner should ensure the allocation complies with treaty permanent-establishment conditions and arm’s length principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section C – Distributions on capital account
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Actual cash distributions, profit distributions, capital returns and any deemed dividend-like amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Since an SCSp is not a company subject to collective CIT, profit withdrawals are not generally subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; report them as partnership draws.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 112: administrative fines loading from EUR 1,000 to EUR 25,000; automatic surcharge up to 10% of any tax determined at partner level; criminal sanctions for deliberate concealment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax for CIT-subject companies; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (holding of at least 10% for 12 months) and 0% for distributions made by an SCSp because the SCSp is not a collective income tax taxpayer and partner profit draws are not dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduction or exemption, the recipient must deliver to the Luxembourg paying agent/withholding agent: (a) an original or certified tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty state, (b) a Luxembourg withholding tax relief application/e-notification through the e-Tax module or the relevant administrative form, and (c) a legal beneficial-ownership declaration. Advance clearance or pre-payment relief is applied through the Luxembourg administration’s ‘exonération à la source’ procedure; a foreign tax credit for any residual Luxembourg WHT is claimed on the partner’s home country return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no withholding tax on ordinary cross-border royalty and interest payments (statutory 0%); treaty rates do not generally create source WHT on interest or royalties paid by a Luxembourg resident to non-residents. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive confirms 0% relief for EU connected companies; anti-abuse rules under ATAD may deny relief where the arrangement lacks economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 (group consolidated turnover in the preceding financial year) triggers mandatory Luxembourg Master File and Local File, with a country-by-country reporting obligation at the same EUR 750 million threshold; Luxembourg-connected entities with controlled transactions below this threshold must still maintain adequate contemporaneous transfer pricing evidence for inspection.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to Cayman/BVI; however, the Luxembourg General Anti-Abuse Rule (ATAD Article 6) and domestic case law require a real economic presence, business purpose, decision-making, adequately risked capital and arm’s length staffing. An SCSp acting as a charitable endowment manager should maintain local substance or clearly documented external mandates; a present- or near-shell entity engaging in treaty-based passive income routing is open to recharacterisation, denial of treaty benefits, DAC6 hallmarks and penal reattribution of income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally misstating the SCSp’s net income, disguising profits as charitable grant expenses, creating false donor/grantee records, or hiding the identity of partners from the Luxembourg tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all under-declared tax; fraud penalty of 50%–150% of the evaded tax; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 or up to 10% of the sum evaded; confiscation of proceeds; imprisonment under Luxembourg fiscal criminal law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, general partners and de facto managers may be jointly and severally liable for tax, penalties and interest; courts may freeze personal assets, impose travel bans and enter custodial sentences after final conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp with no physical office, employees, business records, local bank account or partner decision-making, and using it solely to channel passive income from Luxembourg to a low-tax jurisdiction under a DTA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits; reallocation of profits to the beneficial owners under the Luxembourg GAAR; immediate recapture of exempt income; administrative penalties (commonly up to EUR 100,000) and DAC6/ATAD penalty assessments for undisclosed intermediaries.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where limited liability is disregarded, directors and managers may be treated as co-taxpayers for the unpaid corporate tax; civil restitution extends to avoided dividend withholding tax and interest; serious abuse may trigger travel restrictions during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Breach (Anti-Money Laundering Law of 12 November 2004)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence on donors, funders and grant recipients; accepting suspected proceeds of crime; using the SCSp to exfiltrate assets through apparently charitable grants; non-declaration of beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000,000 for legal persons; criminal penalties of up to 5 years’ imprisonment for natural persons; revocation of the foundation or SPF-like licence; confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for executing forbidden transfers; the court may order civil damages, asset freezes, travel bans and, in serious organised-crime cases, pre-trial detention.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omission of the annual Form 112 or Form 111, late filing, incomplete partner allocations, or knowingly supplying false declaration data on a charitable endowment SCSp.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Automatic tax surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax; late-payment interest at 0.6% per month capped at 10%; administrative fine up to EUR 25,000; repeat intentional omission treated as fiscal fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to ensure regulatory filings may be declared personally liable where the SCSp is insolvent; they may be prohibited from serving as directors and, upon criminal conviction, may face travel bans and imprisonment.
